questions.question: In a triangle PQR, RS intersects PQ at point S. The sides of the triangle QR = 36 cm, SQ = 27 cm, RS = 18 cm and ∠QRS = ∠QPR. What is the ratio of the perimeter of ∆PRS to that of ∆QSR?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a ΔPQR, RS intersects PQ at point S.

QR = 36 cm

SQ = 27 cm

RS = 18 cm

∠QRS = ∠QPR

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d3a1f6c3dc5d2ac7167745e60909afe64b364cc5d11757740c9ee04434fa125.png] 

In triangle PQR and QSR

∠QRS = ∠QPR (Given)

∠Q = ∠Q (Common)

So by AA rule, Δ PQR ∼ ΔQSR,

27/36 = 18/PR

PR = 24 cm

So, (27 + PS) / 36 = 36 / 27

PS = 48 - 27

PS = 21 cm

So, the ratio of the perimeter of ∆PRS to that of ∆QSR:

∆PRS / ∆QSR = (24 + 18 + 21) / (27 + 18 + 36) 

= 63 / 81

= (7)/(9)

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, PQ is a straight line parallel to AC, such that Area ABC : Area PBQ = 3 : 1 Then CB : CQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area Δ ABC : Area Δ PBQ = 3 : 1 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50109e15104c6a853677a4b3e303cc97e14497fee73a098db8606afdeed7134e.png] 

Area of ΔABC/Area of ΔPBQ = 3/1

⇒ CB/BQ = √3/√1 = √3/1

Let CB = √3x and BQ = x

⇒ CQ = CB – BQ = √3x – x = (√3 – 1)x

⇒ CB/CQ = √3x/(√3 – 1)x = √3/(√3 – 1)

⇒ CB/CQ = frac{{surd 3}}{{sqrt 3 - 1}} times frac{{sqrt 3 + 1}}{{sqrt 3 + 1}} = frac{{sqrt 3 ( {sqrt 3 + 1} )}}{2}

∴ CB : CQ = √3(√3 + 1) : 2

**∴ The correct answer is √3(√3 + 1) : 2.**

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle ABC such that ∠BAC = 90° and AD is perpendicular to BC. If the area of ΔABC is 63 cm², area of ΔACD = 7 cm², and AC = 5 cm, then the length of BC is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of ΔABC = 63 cm²

Area of ΔACD = 7 cm²

AC = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔXYZ, then

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔXYZ) = (AB/XY)² = (BC/YZ)2 = (AC/XZ)2

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb956877f6a76bd78a2be16fedfb79b974615ef705dee8dad8fe9661bd687061.png] 

In ΔABC and ΔACD

∠BAC = ∠ADC = 90° 

∠C = ∠C (Common in both triangles)

So, ΔABC ∼ ΔDAC (by AA Similarity)

Now,

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔACD) = (BC/AC)²

⇒ 63/7 = (BC/5)²

⇒ 9/1 = (BC/5)2

⇒ √(9/1) = BC/5

⇒ 3 = BC/5

⇒ BC = 5 × 3 = 15 cm

**∴ The length of BC is 15 cm**

questions.question: In ΔABC, E and D are points on sides AB and AC, respectively, such that ∠ABC = ∠ADE. If AE = 6 cm, AD = 4cm and EB = 4cm, then the length of DC is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AE = 6 cm

AD = 4 cm

EB = 4 cm

and ∠ADE = ∠ABC

**Concept used:**

A-A property of similarity of triangle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/714f87dec88d48000a3db8bf7df4352fac9f048a34a0d3dd94c19dc9325dfed9.png] 

We can see in the ΔABC and ΔADE

Since ∠ADE = ∠ABC and also ∠A is common in both triangle

From A-A property of similarity of triangle:

∴ ΔABC ~ ΔADE

Then, AB/AD = AC/AE

But AC = AD + DC

⇒ AC = 4 + DC

And AB = AE + EB

⇒ AB = 6 + 4

⇒ AB = 10 cm

Now AB/AD = AC/AE

⇒ 10/4 = (4 + DC)/6

⇒ (5/2) × 6 = 4 +DC

⇒ 15 = 4 + DC

⇒ DC = 15 – 4

⇒ DC = 11 cm.

**Hence, Length of DC is 11 cm.**

questions.question: In a ΔABC, AD is perpendicular to BC from A. if ∠BAC = 90°, then AB² : AC² is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71af5dfbc16c326a840f004aa36424b51fc553af27d667896ca2143595ea0e4a.png] 

In ∆ABC and ∆ DBA

∠ABC = ∠DBA

∠ACB = ∠DAB

∴ ∆ ABC ~ ∆ DBA

∴ AB/BD = BC/AB

⇒ AB² 
= BD × BC …(1)

In ∆ ABC and ∆ CAD

∠ABC = ∠CAD

∠ACB = ∠DCA

∴ ∆ ABC ~ ∆ CAD

∴ AC/CD = BC/AC

⇒ AC² = CD × BC …(2)

Dividing eq..(1) by eq..(2)

AB²/AC² = (BD × BC)/(BC × CD)

⇒ AB²/AC² = BD/CD

∴ AB² : AC² = BD : CD
